messages.content: You are BioGPT, an expert compiler architect. Translate the provided natural language biological protocol into valid, deterministic BioScript code for execution on a microfluidic biochip.

Source link: https://ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4255744
Paper DOI: https://doi.org/10.1186/1471-2105-15-S14-S5

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: EXACT2-Formalized Worked Example Protocol Fragment ("Adjust to 10% TCA. Incubate at 30 C overnight.")

REAGENTS/OBJECTS USED:
  - Sample (the biochemical entity being adjusted/incubated; left unspecified in the paper's own worked example -- Figure 3's output explicitly records "Biochemical entity: not found")
  - TCA Solution (10% Trichloroacetic acid, NCBI PubChem CID 6421)

STEPS (as identified and disambiguated by the EXACT2 Translator engine, Figures 2-3):
1. Sentence 1 / Adjust: adjust the sample to 10% Trichloroacetic acid (TCA is recognized as an abbreviation and normalized to "Trichloroacetic acid", assigned NCBI PubChem ID CID 6421).
2. Sentence 2 / Incubate: incubate the (adjusted) sample at 30 C. The descriptor temperature is recognized directly from the "30 C" clue in the text (assigned Units Ontology ID UO:0000027). The descriptor period is disambiguated from the ambiguous term "overnight" to a concrete value of 16 hours, per the framework's lab-specific default settings (ON = 16 hours). The descriptors biochemical entity and condition are noted by the Translator engine's own output as "not found" -- i.e., essential information missing from the original text that the framework would prompt a human user to supply.

INTERPRETATION: This worked example is used by the paper to demonstrate the EXACT2-based translation framework converting an ambiguous natural-language protocol sentence pair into a semantically defined, machine-processable representation. It illustrates two of EXACT2's core capabilities: (1) resolving lab-specific abbreviations and ambiguous time expressions (TCA, "overnight") into disambiguated, ID-linked values, and (2) explicitly flagging essential descriptors (here, the biochemical entity being incubated and the incubation condition) that are missing from the original text and must be supplied by a user or inferred from context (e.g., from a preceding "yeast growth culture" step) for the protocol to be reproducible.

source.title: EXACT2-Formalized Worked Example Protocol Fragment ("Adjust to 10% TCA. Incubate at 30 C overnight.")

ir.content:
main:
	s1[0] = dispense(sample)
	tca1[0] = dispense(tca_solution)
	adjusted1[0] = mix(s1[0], tca1[0])
	heat(adjusted1[0]) @ 30.0CELSIUS @ 57600.0SECOND
	dispose(adjusted1[0])
	NOP

numeric_mismatches.note: BioScript has no dedicated concentration-adjustment primitive corresponding to EXACT2's <adjust> experimental action, so combining the sample with the TCA solution is represented with 'mix', the nearest available operation.

The paper's own worked example explicitly reports the biochemical entity being incubated as not found in the source text; this is a documented gap in the original protocol fragment, not an assumption added by this translation.

The source text says only 'overnight', which is inherently ambiguous (the paper notes it can mean 12-18+ hours depending on lab). The value used here (16 hours) is the paper's own stated default disambiguation for the abbreviation ON, not an independently chosen figure.
